morning.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
morning.transliteration: Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika amsaynā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykan-nushūr.
morning.translation: O Allah, by You we reach the morning, and by You we reach the evening; by You we live, and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.

evening.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ
evening.transliteration: Allāhumma bika amsaynā, wa bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykal-maṣīr.
evening.translation: O Allah, by You we reach the evening, and by You we reach the morning; by You we live, and by You we die, and to You is the final return.

duas.reference: Al-Adab al-Mufrad of al-Bukhari (no. 1199), at-Tirmidhi (no. 3391) — graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
duas.transliteration: Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwal-Ḥayyul-Qayyūm, lā ta'khudhuhū sinatun wa lā nawm, lahū mā fis-samāwāti wa mā fil-arḍ. Man dhal-ladhī yashfa'u 'indahū illā bi'idhnih. Ya'lamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum, wa lā yuḥīṭūna bishay'im-min 'ilmihī illā bimā shā'a, wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samāwāti wal-arḍ, wa lā ya'ūduhū ḥifẓuhumā, wa huwal-'Aliyyul-'Aẓīm.
duas.translation: Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Ever-Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except with His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Footstool extends over the heavens and the earth, and He does not tire in guarding and preserving them. And He is the Most High, the Most Great. (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:255 — Ayat al-Kursi)
duas.virtue: Whoever recites it in the morning will be protected from the jinn until the evening, and whoever recites it in the evening will be protected from them until the morning.
duas.reference: Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/562), authenticated by al-Albani in Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib (1/673).

duas.arabic:
قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ * ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ * لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ * وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ * مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ * وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ * وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَـٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ * وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ * مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ * إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ * مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ * ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ * مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
duas.transliteration: Qul huwallāhu aḥad, Allāhuṣ-ṣamad, lam yalid wa lam yūlad, wa lam yakul-lahū kufuwan aḥad. Qul a'ūdhu birabbil-falaq, min sharri mā khalaq, wa min sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqab, wa min sharrin-naffāthāti fil-'uqad, wa min sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasad. Qul a'ūdhu birabbin-nās, malikin-nās, ilāhin-nās, min sharril-waswāsil-khannās, alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūrin-nās, minal-jinnati wan-nās.
duas.translation: Surah al-Ikhlas: "Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Self-Sufficient Master. He begets not, nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him." Surah al-Falaq: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies." Surah an-Nas: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, from among the jinn and mankind."
duas.reference: Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi, graded sahih by al-Albani in Sahih at-Tirmidhi (3/182).

morning.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَـٰذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَـٰذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
morning.transliteration: Aṣbaḥnā wa aṣbaḥal-mulku lillāh, walḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu wa huwa 'alā kulli shay'in qadīr. Rabbi as'aluka khayra mā fī hādhal-yawmi wa khayra mā ba'dah, wa a'ūdhu bika min sharri mā fī hādhal-yawmi wa sharri mā ba'dah. Rabbi a'ūdhu bika minal-kasali wa sū'il-kibar. Rabbi a'ūdhu bika min 'adhābin fin-nāri wa 'adhābin fil-qabr.
morning.translation: We have entered the morning, and with it all dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is due to Allah. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion, to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things capable. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and feeble old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.

evening.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَـٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَـٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
evening.transliteration: Amsaynā wa amsal-mulku lillāh, walḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu wa huwa 'alā kulli shay'in qadīr. Rabbi as'aluka khayra mā fī hādhihil-laylati wa khayra mā ba'dahā, wa a'ūdhu bika min sharri mā fī hādhihil-laylati wa sharri mā ba'dahā. Rabbi a'ūdhu bika minal-kasali wa sū'il-kibar. Rabbi a'ūdhu bika min 'adhābin fin-nāri wa 'adhābin fil-qabr.
evening.translation: We have entered the evening, and with it all dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is due to Allah. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion, to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things capable. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and feeble old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.

duas.reference: Morning wording: Sahih Muslim (no. 2723). Evening wording: at-Tirmidhi (no. 3390), graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَىٰ عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
duas.transliteration: Allāhumma anta Rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa ana 'abduk, wa ana 'alā 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastaṭa't. A'ūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣana't. Abū'u laka bini'matika 'alayy, wa abū'u bidhanbī, faghfir lī fa'innahū lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant.
duas.translation: O Allah, You are my Lord, none has the right to be worshipped but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
duas.virtue: This is the master of seeking forgiveness (sayyid al-istighfar). Whoever says it during the day with firm conviction and dies that day before evening will be among the people of Paradise, and whoever says it at night with firm conviction and dies before morning will be among the people of Paradise.
duas.reference: Al-Bukhari (no. 6306), an-Nasa'i (no. 9752), at-Tirmidhi (no. 3391).

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي بَدَنِي، اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي سَمْعِي، اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي بَصَرِي، لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْفَقْرِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ، لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
duas.transliteration: Allāhumma 'āfinī fī badanī, Allāhumma 'āfinī fī sam'ī, Allāhumma 'āfinī fī baṣarī, lā ilāha illā ant. Allāhumma innī a'ūdhu bika minal-kufri wal-faqr, wa a'ūdhu bika min 'adhābil-qabr, lā ilāha illā ant.
duas.translation: O Allah, grant my body wellbeing. O Allah, grant my hearing wellbeing. O Allah, grant my sight wellbeing. None has the right to be worshipped but You. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. None has the right to be worshipped but You.
duas.reference: Abu Dawud (no. 5090), Ahmad (5/42), an-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah (no. 22), Ibn as-Sunni (no. 69), al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad — isnad graded hasan by al-Albani, and by Ibn Baz in Tuhfat al-Akhyar (p. 26).

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي، اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي، اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ وَمِنْ خَلْفِي وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي وَمِنْ فَوْقِي، وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي
duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'alukal-'afwa wal-'āfiyata fid-dunyā wal-ākhirah. Allāhumma innī as'alukal-'afwa wal-'āfiyata fī dīnī wa dunyāya wa ahlī wa mālī. Allāhummastur 'awrātī wa āmin raw'ātī. Allāhummaḥfaẓnī min bayni yadayya wa min khalfī wa 'an yamīnī wa 'an shimālī wa min fawqī, wa a'ūdhu bi'aẓamatika an ughtāla min taḥtī.
duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in my religious and worldly affairs, and my family and my wealth. O Allah, conceal my faults and set at ease my fears. O Allah, guard me from before me, from behind me, from my right, from my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being taken unawares from beneath me.
duas.reference: Abu Dawud (no. 5074), Ibn Majah (no. 3871), al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad (no. 1200) — graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ، وَأَنْ أَقْتَرِفَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِي سُوءًا أَوْ أَجُرَّهُ إِلَىٰ مُسْلِمٍ
duas.transliteration: Allāhumma 'ālimal-ghaybi wash-shahādati fāṭiras-samāwāti wal-arḍ, Rabba kulli shay'in wa malīkah. Ash-hadu al-lā ilāha illā ant. A'ūdhu bika min sharri nafsī wa min sharrish-shayṭāni wa shirkih, wa an aqtarifa 'alā nafsī sū'an aw ajurrahū ilā muslim.
duas.translation: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul and from the evil of Satan and his associates, and from bringing evil upon myself or driving it towards another Muslim.
duas.reference: The Messenger of Allah instructed Abu Bakr to recite this. At-Tirmidhi (no. 3529), Abu Dawud (no. 5067), al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad (no. 1204) — graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
duas.transliteration: Bismillāhil-ladhī lā yaḍurru ma'as-mihī shay'un fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samā'i wa huwas-Samī'ul-'Alīm.
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
duas.virtue: Whoever recites this three times in the morning and three times in the evening, nothing will harm him.
duas.reference: Abu Dawud (no. 5088), at-Tirmidhi (no. 3388), Ibn Majah (no. 3869), al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad (no. 660) — graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَبِيًّا
duas.transliteration: Raḍītu billāhi rabban, wa bil-Islāmi dīnan, wa bi-Muḥammadin ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallama nabiyyan.
duas.translation: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muhammad (peace be upon him) as my Prophet.
duas.virtue: It is a right upon Allah that He will be pleased with whoever says this on the Day of Resurrection; in one narration, Paradise is guaranteed for the one who recites it.
duas.reference: Abu Dawud (no. 1529), Ibn Majah (no. 3870), at-Tirmidhi (no. 3389), Ahmad (4/337) — graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّومُ، بِرَحْمَتِكَ أَسْتَغِيثُ، أَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ، وَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَىٰ نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ
duas.transliteration: Yā Ḥayyu yā Qayyūm, bi-raḥmatika astaghīth, aṣliḥ lī sha'nī kullah, wa lā takilnī ilā nafsī ṭarfata 'ayn.
duas.translation: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help. Set right all of my affairs, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
duas.reference: An-Nasa'i in as-Sunan al-Kubra (6/147), al-Hakim (1/730) who graded it sahih, adh-Dhahabi agreed, and al-Albani in Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib (1/273).

morning.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا عَلَىٰ فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَعَلَىٰ كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ، وَعَلَىٰ دِينِ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَعَلَىٰ مِلَّةِ أَبِينَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ
morning.transliteration: Aṣbaḥnā 'alā fiṭratil-Islām, wa 'alā kalimatil-ikhlāṣ, wa 'alā dīni nabiyyinā Muḥammadin ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam, wa 'alā millati abīnā Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan musliman, wa mā kāna minal-mushrikīn.
morning.translation: We have entered the morning upon the natural religion of Islam, upon the word of sincere devotion, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, a man of pure faith and submission, who was not among those who associate partners with Allah.

evening.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا عَلَىٰ فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَعَلَىٰ كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ، وَعَلَىٰ دِينِ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَعَلَىٰ مِلَّةِ أَبِينَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ
evening.transliteration: Amsaynā 'alā fiṭratil-Islām, wa 'alā kalimatil-ikhlāṣ, wa 'alā dīni nabiyyinā Muḥammadin ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam, wa 'alā millati abīnā Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan musliman, wa mā kāna minal-mushrikīn.
evening.translation: We have entered the evening upon the natural religion of Islam, upon the word of sincere devotion, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, a man of pure faith and submission, who was not among those who associate partners with Allah.

duas.reference: Ahmad (3/406, 407 and 5/123), Ibn as-Sunni in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah (no. 34) — authenticated by al-Albani, see Sahih al-Jami' (no. 8803).

duas.translation: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.
duas.virtue: No one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than this, except one who has said the same or more.
duas.reference: Sahih Muslim (no. 2692).

duas.arabic: لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
duas.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamd, wa huwa 'alā kulli shay'in qadīr.
duas.translation: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things capable.
duas.virtue: Whoever recites this ten times is credited with the reward of freeing four slaves from the descendants of Isma'il, ten good deeds are recorded for him, ten sins are wiped away, and he is raised ten ranks and protected from Satan until evening (or morning). A related version with the wording "yuḥyī wa yumīt" ("He gives life and causes death") is recited ten times after Maghrib for the same protection through the night.
duas.reference: An-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah (no. 24), al-Albani in Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib (1/272); Abu Dawud (no. 5077), graded sahih by al-Albani. Maghrib version: reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and at-Tirmidhi (no. 3534), graded hasan by al-Albani.

duas.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
duas.transliteration: Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdihī 'adada khalqihī, wa riḍā nafsihī, wa zinata 'arshihī, wa midāda kalimātih.
duas.translation: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, by the number of His creation, by His own pleasure, by the weight of His Throne, and by the extent of His words.
duas.virtue: The reward for this exceeds that of many other remembrances.
duas.reference: Sahih Muslim (no. 2726).

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا، وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'aluka 'ilman nāfi'an, wa rizqan ṭayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan.
duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and deeds that are accepted.
duas.reference: Ibn Majah (no. 925), graded sahih by al-Albani.

duas.translation: I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.
duas.virtue: The Prophet (peace be upon him) himself sought Allah's forgiveness one hundred times a day, and in one narration said he did so more than that.
duas.reference: Sahih Muslim (no. 2702); al-Bukhari (no. 6307).

morning.arabic: أَصْبَحْتُ أُثْنِي عَلَيْكَ حَمْدًا، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
morning.transliteration: Aṣbaḥtu uthnī 'alayka ḥamdan, wa ash-hadu al-lā ilāha illallāh.
morning.translation: I have entered the morning praising You, and I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah.

evening.arabic: أَمْسَيْتُ أُثْنِي عَلَيْكَ حَمْدًا، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
evening.transliteration: Amsaytu uthnī 'alayka ḥamdan, wa ash-hadu al-lā ilāha illallāh.
evening.translation: I have entered the evening praising You, and I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah.

duas.reference: 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah of Imam an-Nasa'i (p. 382; as-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 10331) — graded hasan by Shaikh Muqbil ibn Hadi al-Wadi'i in al-Jami' as-Sahih (2/473).

duas.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
duas.transliteration: A'ūdhu bikalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
duas.translation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
duas.virtue: Whoever recites this three times in the evening will not be harmed by the sting of any poisonous creature that night. Also reported that reciting it once upon stopping at a place protects from harm until moving on.
duas.reference: Ibn Majah (no. 3518), graded sahih by al-Albani; Sahih Muslim (no. 2709).

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَىٰ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَىٰ آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَىٰ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَىٰ آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
duas.transliteration: Allāhumma ṣalli 'alā Muḥammadin wa 'alā āli Muḥammadin kamā ṣallayta 'alā Ibrāhīma wa 'alā āli Ibrāhīma innaka Ḥamīdum-Majīd. Allāhumma bārik 'alā Muḥammadin wa 'alā āli Muḥammadin kamā bārakta 'alā Ibrāhīma wa 'alā āli Ibrāhīma innaka Ḥamīdum-Majīd.
duas.translation: O Allah, send praise upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent praise upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, send blessing upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessing upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.
duas.virtue: Whoever sends this salah upon the Prophet once, Allah will send tenfold blessing upon him, erase ten sins from him, and raise him ten ranks.
duas.reference: Abu Dawud (no. 978), graded sahih by al-Albani; an-Nasa'i (no. 1297), graded sahih by al-Albani.
